title: Error of a depth-zero randomized tree
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\pi$ be a probability law on $\Omega$. Suppose $f:(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$ takes only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every tree selected by the randomized tree’s finite nonempty seed space is a single leaf. Then the smaller of the probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and $-1$ is at most the tree’s error probability under the product law induced by $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: The randomized tree has a finite nonempty seed space with a probability law
$f$ is a real-valued function on $n$-coordinate inputs
For every seed, the selected tree is a single leaf
